title: Therapeutic gases and the Nrf2/Keap1 pathway: direct thiol modification vs. indirect modulation

license.text: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/This is an open access article distributed under the Creative Commons Attribution License 4.0 (CCBY), which permits unrestricted use, distribution, and reproduction in any medium, provided the original work is properly cited. http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0.

paragraphs.en: Aerobic life depends on tightly regulated redox chemistry. Reactive oxygen species and reactive nitrogen species are not merely toxic by-products of metabolism; at physiological levels, they function as second messengers that shape proliferation, differentiation, immunity, metabolism, and tissue repair.1 Oxidative distress emerges when the rate, location, or persistence of reactive species exceeds the buffering capacity of antioxidant and repair systems, causing damage to lipids, proteins, and nucleic acids.2 Because this transition from signaling to injury is controlled rather than accidental, cellular defense systems must continuously discriminate between useful redox inputs and harmful ones.3

The best-studied coordinator of that discrimination is the nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (Nrf2)/Kelch-like Ech-associated protein 1 (Keap1) pathway. Under homeostatic conditions, Keap1 acts as a cysteine-rich substrate adaptor that promotes cullin 3 (Cul3)-dependent ubiquitination and proteasomal turnover of Nrf2. Under oxidative or electrophilic challenge, strategically placed Keap1 cysteines change their reactivity and conformation, reducing Nrf2 degradation, enabling nuclear accumulation, and inducing a transcriptional program that includes antioxidant enzymes, glutathione synthesis machinery, detoxification systems, and genes involved in proteostasis, intermediary metabolism, and mitochondrial function.34 Because of this architecture, the pathway acts less like an on-off switch than like a biochemical sensor array that decodes a spectrum of redox states into adaptive transcriptional outputs.56

Therapeutic interest in gaseous small molecules grew from a different historical direction. Nitric oxide and hydrogen sulfide (H2S) entered mainstream biology as endogenous gasotransmitters, while molecular hydrogen was initially considered biologically inert until reports suggested selective protective effects against highly reactive oxidants.789 The three molecules differ profoundly in redox potential, bond chemistry, endogenous production, and pharmacokinetics. Nitric oxide (NO) is a radical, H2S is a nucleophilic/reducing sulfur species whose biological actions often proceed through reactive sulfur intermediates, and molecular hydrogen (H2) is a stable, nonpolar diatomic molecule with unusually high diffusibility but limited direct chemical reactivity.1011 That contrast makes their repeated convergence on antioxidant and cytoprotective phenotypes scientifically intriguing rather than self-evident.

Most reviews still treat these gases separately. That approach is useful for cataloguing biosynthesis, canonical targets, and disease-specific studies, but it can obscure a deeper question: how can chemically distinct gases converge functionally on one stress-response hub? A comparative Nrf2-centered analysis provides a way to answer that question because Keap1-Nrf2 sits at the intersection of thiol chemistry, electrophile sensing, mitochondrial adaptation, inflammatory tone, and metabolic remodeling.1213 It is therefore an ideal framework for distinguishing direct covalent mechanisms from indirect network effects.

This review develops four arguments. First, NO and H2S activate Nrf2 primarily through direct or near-direct mechanisms involving cysteine modification, although the exact residue preference and downstream consequences depend on the local redox context. Second, H2 appears to influence the pathway mainly through indirect remodeling of upstream oxidative events, mitochondrial electron leakage, and secondary electrophile formation, rather than through a defined direct receptor-like interaction.1114 Third, all three gases converge on a shared layer of kinase signaling, proteostasis, and mitochondrial quality control that amplifies or stabilizes Nrf2 responses. Fourth, translational progress will likely depend less on maximizing gas dose and more on matching the right gas, timing, and delivery system to the right disease context. The purpose of this expanded review is therefore not simply to summarize gas biology, but to compare mechanistic logics and identify the degree to which multi-gas strategies are conceptually justified (Figure 1).

A structured search of PubMed, Web of Science Core Collection, and Scopus was conducted from database inception to May 20, 2026. Search terms included “ Nrf2,” “NFE2L2,” “Keap1,” “nitric oxide,” “hydrogen sulfide,” “molecular hydrogen,” “gasotransmitter,” “S-nitrosylation,” “persulfidation,” “redox signaling,” “mitochondrial function,” “oxidative stress,” and “drug delivery.” Reference lists of relevant articles were also screened. English-language, peer-reviewed studies addressing NO, H2S, or H2 in relation to Nrf2/Keap1 signaling, redox regulation, mitochondrial function, disease applications, or delivery strategies were included. Duplicate records, conference abstracts, editorials, non-English publications, and studies lacking mechanistic or translational relevance were excluded. Recent studies were prioritized, while landmark earlier publications were retained when necessary.

sections.title: The Nrf2/Keap1 Axis Is a Cysteine-Sensitive Signaling Hub

paragraphs.en: Nrf2 belongs to the Cap‘n’collar basic leucine zipper family and orchestrates a transcriptional network centered on antioxidant response elements. The importance of the pathway is no longer confined to classic phase II detoxification. Nrf2 also influences glutamine utilization, nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide phosphate production, iron handling, proteasomal function, autophagy, mitochondrial biogenesis, and inflammatory set points.34

The canonical mechanism of pathway repression has become a paradigmatic example of thiol-based stress sensing. Keap1 is a dimeric protein containing an N-terminal BTB domain, an intervening region rich in reactive cysteines, and a Kelch domain that binds Nrf2. In basal conditions, one Keap1 dimer engages a single Nrf2 molecule through high-affinity and low-affinity motifs, presenting Nrf2 for Cul3-mediated ubiquitination. Electrophiles or oxidants alter selected Keap1 cysteines and disrupt this efficient turnover cycle, allowing newly synthesized Nrf2 to escape degradation and accumulate in the nucleus.345

The so-called cysteine code is especially relevant for gas biology. Keap1 contains many cysteines, but they are not equivalent. Cys151 is particularly associated with sensing reactive electrophiles and changes near the BTB-Cul3 interface, whereas Cys273 and Cys288 often emerge in models involving larger conformational effects on substrate orientation and repression efficiency.345

A comparative review centered on NO, H2S, and H2 must also consider noncanonical activation. p62/sequestosome1 can compete with Nrf2 for Keap1 binding when autophagic flux changes, thereby stabilizing Nrf2 independently of direct cysteine oxidation. In addition, glycogen synthase kinase 3 (GSK-3) can promote β-transducin repeatcontaining protein-dependent Nrf2 degradation through a Keap1-independent route, while adenosine monophosphateactivated protein kinase (AMPK) and other kinases modulate Nrf2 localization and activity under nutrient and energetic stress.151617

The translational consequence of this architecture is important. Nrf2 activation is beneficial in many acute injury settings, but indiscriminate or chronic activation can also create liabilities, including reductive imbalance, altered immune tone, and in some contexts support of malignant cell survival.46 Therefore, the therapeutic question is not whether gas-mediated Nrf2 activation occurs, but under what timing, dose, and disease stage it helps rather than harms.

sections.title: Nitric Oxide and Hydrogen Sulfide Direct Modulate Nrf2/Keap1 Axis

paragraphs.en: NO is generated endogenously by nitric oxide synthases, diffuses rapidly across membranes, and participates in vasodilation, neurotransmission, platelet regulation, and host defense. Yet the same molecule can contribute to nitrative injury when produced in excess or when rapidly converted to secondary species such as peroxynitrite.718 In Nrf2, the most direct mechanism is S-nitrosylation of reactive cysteines on Keap1. NO and NO-derived nitrosating equivalents can modify Keap1, weaken its repression of Nrf2, and promote transcription of cytoprotective genes.1920 NO rarely acts alone in biological systems. Crosstalk with phosphatidylinositol 3kinase (PI3K)/protein kinase B (Akt), extracellular signalregulated kinase 1/2, and AMPK can amplify Nrf2 stabilization, while changes in cyclic guanosine monophosphate signaling, endothelial shear stress responses, and mitochondrial respiration alter Nrf2.1321 Consequently, the protective phenotype attributed to NO often represents the sum of direct S-nitrosylation, kinase-mediated signal propagation, and vascular-hemodynamic improvement rather than one isolated molecular event. NO promotes S-nitrosylation-dependent relaxation of Keap1 repression than implying that dissolved NO directly binds a unique molecular receptor on Keap1.1920 The biological meaning of NO-dependent Nrf2 activation also depends on concentration and timing. At moderate levels, the pathway contributes to vascular protection, anti-inflammatory feedback, and adaptation to transient stress. Under severe inflammatory or ischemia-reperfusion conditions, however, simultaneous superoxide production shifts NO chemistry toward peroxynitrite formation, protein tyrosine nitration, and mitochondrial dysfunction.18 This complexity explains why NO remains a double-edged therapeutic candidate. Very short half-life, steep dose-response behavior, high susceptibility to oxidative consumption, and systemic hypotensive risk all constrain clinical implementation.

H2S is often described as a gasotransmitter analogous to NO, yet its chemistry is distinct. H2S exists in equilibrium with hydrosulfide ion (HS−) and participates in a broader reactive sulfur species network rather than acting solely as a free dissolved gas. Its effects depend on enzymatic production, mitochondrial sulfide oxidation, local pH, metal centers, disulfides, and sulfur-transfer reactions.8910 These features make H2S particularly suited to modifying thiols and sulfur-rich protein microenvironments.

Several studies support the view that H2S donors or endogenous H2S-generating systems promote Keap1 persulfidation, reduce repression of Nrf2, and enhance antioxidant gene expression.22 In acute injury settings, controlled H2S delivery can lower energy demand, attenuate oxidative bursts, preserve endothelial function, and indirectly sustain Nrf2-dependent defense programs. In chronic settings, H2S has been linked to vascular homeostasis, anti-inflammatory feedback, and improved redox resilience.821 For translational design, H2S thus appears less as a generic antioxidant and more as a controllable thiol-modifying cue with a relatively strong mechanistic bridge to Nrf2/Keap1.

NO and H2S react chemically and influence each other’s biosynthesis, degradation, and signaling outputs. The resulting network includes hybrid reactive sulfur-nitrogen species, such as HSNO and SSNO−, along with downstream shifts in nitrosothiol and persulfide pools.123

HSNO has attracted particular attention because it is small, membrane permeable, and capable of transferring nitroso or sulfur-related reactivity depending on context.2324 Although some intermediate species are transient and difficult to quantify in vivo, the broader conclusion is well supported: NO-H2S interactions generate chemically distinct products that can redistribute signaling competence across membranes and protein thiols. In practical terms, this means that co-exposure to NO and H2S is not simply additive; it can qualitatively change the redox species landscape encountered by Keap1 and other signaling proteins (Figure 2).

For Nrf2, the important point is not that every proposed intermediate has been definitively mapped in vivo, but that NO and H2S can reshape each other’s access to the thiol network. Nitrosylation may be converted, buffered, or redirected by sulfur chemistry, while persulfidation states can alter sensitivity to additional oxidation or nitrosation.1025

The vascular system provides a particularly intuitive example. Endothelial health depends on balanced NO bioavailability, mitochondrial competence, and suppression of chronic oxidative stress. H2S has been reported to support endothelial function and NO signaling partly by lowering oxidative burden and influencing endothelial NO synthase coupling, whereas NO can modulate enzymes involved in sulfur metabolism and vascular tone.2125 Nrf2 becomes a systems integrator in this setting because it links both gas pathways to antioxidant transcription, glutathione homeostasis, and endothelial stress adaptation. At the same time, most evidence remains preclinical, mechanistically heterogeneous.

sections.title: Molecular Hydrogen Indirectly Regulates Nrf2/Keap1 Axis

paragraphs.en: H2 is electrically neutral, nonpolar, and kinetically stable under physiological conditions. It lacks the overt thiol-reactive chemistry that makes NO and H2S natural candidates for Keap1 modification. Yet a substantial literature describes anti-inflammatory, anti-apoptotic, and antioxidant-like effects of H2 across organ injury, neurological disease, metabolic dysfunction, and exercise-related stress.91426

One influential hypothesis is that H2 attenuates runaway free-radical chain reactions in membranes while allowing limited generation of secondary electrophilic mediators, including oxidized phospholipid derivatives and 4-hydroxynonenal, that can themselves activate adaptive signaling programs.2728 In this model, H2 does not directly oxidize or reduce Keap1. Instead, it changes the quality and quantity of upstream oxidative events, thereby shifting the electrophile landscape presented to the Keap1 sensor system.

Since H2 diffuses rapidly into subcellular compartments, it is well positioned to influence local redox dynamics at the level of the electron transport chain. Several authors have proposed that H2 reduces pathological electron leakage, improves respiratory efficiency under stress, and secondarily alters NAD+/NADH balance, Sirt1 activity, and downstream transcriptional programs linked to stress resistance and mitochondrial biogenesis.111429

The link to Nrf2 is therefore probably indirect but biologically coherent. If H2 lowers pathological electron leakage, reshapes lipid oxidation products, or improves energetic signaling, it can influence AMPK, PI3K/Akt, GSK-3, and autophagy-related pathways that determine Nrf2 stabilization and transcriptional output.151617

An additional reason H2 remains therapeutically attractive is its unusually broad safety window. Unlike NO and H2S, H2 does not usually exhibit a narrow biphasic toxicity threshold under normobaric therapeutic conditions, and it can be administered through inhalation, hydrogen-rich water, hydrogen-rich saline, or emerging carrier platforms (Figure 3 and Table 1).263031

sections.title: Nrf2/Kaep1 Axis as a Shared Signal Axis for Gas Treatment

paragraphs.en: While direct Keap1 modification is strong for NO and H2S, H2 engages this redox layer indirectly by reshaping the membrane lipid oxidation landscape. This shifts the production of secondary mediators, such as 4-hydroxynonenal and oxidized phospholipids, which then act as the proximal triggers for Keap1. Importantly, NO and H2S also intersect with these networks, generating reactive species like nitrated fatty acids, making lipid-derived electrophiles a shared mechanistic bridge to Nrf2 across all three gases. PI3K/Akt, extracellular signalregulated kinase 1/2, p38 mitogen-activated protein kinase, and AMPK repeatedly appear across gas studies as amplifiers or stabilizers of Nrf2 responses.1317

The PI3K/Akt-GSK-3 axis is especially important because it links survival signaling, nutrient state, and oxidative stress. Inhibition of GSK-3 reduces β-transducin repeatcontaining protein-mediated Nrf2 degradation, thereby complementing canonical Keap1 disengagement.16 NO can engage survival kinases through endothelial and receptor-linked pathways; H2S influences kinase signaling through both redox and mitochondrial routes; and H2 is often proposed to stabilize Nrf2 chiefly by improving energetic signaling and limiting maladaptive reactive oxygen species (ROS) amplification.81121

p62 accumulation or altered autophagic flux can sequester Keap1 and produce noncanonical Nrf2 activation.15 At the same time, Nrf2 feeds back on proteasomal capacity, glutathione synthesis, and detoxification pathways that help maintain protein quality control.

Nrf2 regulates genes linked to nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide phosphate generation, iron-sulfur balance, mitochondrial biogenesis, and in some contexts mitophagy.3233 Gas-mediated Nrf2 activation therefore has consequences beyond antioxidant enzyme induction. NO modulates respiration and vascular oxygen delivery, H2S interacts directly with mitochondrial sulfur metabolism and cytochrome c oxidase, and H2 is repeatedly associated with improved mitochondrial efficiency or reduced injury propagation.811
NO and H2S exert specific, well-characterized effects on transcription factors and chromatin-associated proteins through direct nitrosylation and persulfidation, respectively.102027

Taken together, the question is whether distinct upstream chemistries can stabilize overlapping adaptive attractor states (stable, self-sustaining configurations of cellular networks) centered on Nrf2, mitochondrial resilience, and proteostasis. Current evidence supports broader systems-level convergence (Figure 4).

Nrf2/Keap1 is a central node in this network because it translates all three input classes into a common adaptive language: transcription of antioxidant, detoxification, metabolic, and proteostatic genes. However, the network model also emphasizes asymmetry. The three gases are not interchangeable. NO is fast, locally intense, and highly context sensitive. H2S is chemically rich but dose constrained. H2 is pharmacologically forgiving but mechanistically diffuse. As a result, the practical value of a combination strategy is likely to depend on whether the clinical problem requires rapid local signaling, sustained thiol protection, broad tissue penetration, or some temporally staged combination of these features. These are plausible, biologically grounded strategies, but they remain hypotheses or early translational concepts in most disease settings.

Ischemia-reperfusion injury remains one of the clearest contexts in which an Nrf2-centered gas framework has translational appeal. Ischemia depletes ATP and primes mitochondria for burst ROS generation upon reperfusion, while microvascular dysfunction and inflammation further amplify injury.34 H2S has been explored as a metabolic suppressor or preconditioning signal during the ischemic phase, NO as a modulator of perfusion and endothelial function during reperfusion, and H2 as a broadly distributed attenuator of oxidative propagation with a favorable safety profile.830 Within an Nrf2 framework, these interventions may act at different temporal stages of the same injury cascade rather than competing for the same mechanistic niche.

In neurodegenerative diseases, the appeal of H2 is strengthened by its diffusibility and ability to reach the central nervous system via the routes of simple administration.2135 Yet, NO and H2S pathways are also deeply involved in neurovascular coupling, inflammation, and synaptic redox regulation. The challenge is that the brain is exquisitely sensitive to both oxidative stress and inappropriate nitrosative or sulfide exposure. A network view suggests that broad, low-risk H2 exposure may be best positioned as a background modulator, whereas NO or H2S interventions may require targeted or donor-based delivery to avoid systemic liabilities while still engaging Nrf2-related resilience pathways.

Metabolic disease and aging provide a different translational landscape. These conditions often feature low-grade chronic inflammation, impaired mitochondrial flexibility, and blunted adaptive stress responses, including attenuated Nrf2 signaling with age.36 Here, the goal may not be strong acute activation but long-term restoration of redox responsiveness. H2 has attracted attention because long-term intake appears feasible, while H2S donors may help preserve vascular and mitochondrial function if release kinetics are controlled.2937 The Nrf2 axis is attractive in this context because it coordinates redox defense with intermediary metabolism rather than acting as a purely antioxidant endpoint.

Cardiovascular and endothelial disorders also illustrate the value of comparative thinking. Endothelial dysfunction reflects not only oxidant excess but also impaired NO bioavailability, inflammatory activation, and mitochondrial stress. H2S and NO interact directly in the vascular compartment, while H2 may preserve signaling competence by reducing oxidative consumption of NO-related intermediates under stress.2125 If Nrf2 induction accompanies these effects, then vascular benefit may emerge from combined improvement in signaling tone, antioxidant capacity, and mitochondrial integrity rather than from any single gas action (Table 2).

sections.title: Clinical Translation of Nrf2-Centered Gas Framework

paragraphs.en: The main barrier to clinical translation is not conceptual scarcity but delivery control. Gases are small, diffusible, and often short-lived. That makes them attractive biologically but difficult pharmacologically. Inhalation can produce rapid systemic exposure but may be impractical or unsafe for some molecules and settings. Donor compounds can provide localized release but introduce by-products, release kinetics, and tissue specificity as additional variables.303738

The dosing problem is particularly acute for NO and H2S. Both exhibit steep therapeutic windows. Too little exposure may fail to engage protective signaling; too much may worsen hypotension, mitochondrial inhibition, or nitrative injury.818 Gas therapy requires a concentration-time profile that is sufficient to trigger adaptive signaling but insufficient to collapse physiological gradients or generate toxic secondary chemistry. Nrf2 activation itself follows this logic: transient and appropriately scaled activation is often beneficial, whereas excessive or chronic activation can become maladaptive.6

H2 differs because its safety margin is broader, but this does not eliminate delivery questions. Concentration at target tissue, duration of dissolved H2, and route-specific kinetics still affect biological output. Hydrogen-rich water is convenient but variable in dose delivery; inhalation offers better control but different practical constraints; emerging carriers aim to prolong retention or localize release.2631 Because H2 likely acts indirectly, timing relative to the evolving injury process may matter as much as absolute concentration.

Advanced delivery systems are therefore central to the future of the field. Nanocarriers, gas-releasing molecules, hybrid donor systems, and stimuli-responsive platforms are being developed to transform diffuse gas exposure into more programmable pharmacology.3839 For NO and H2S, responsive systems may reduce burst toxicity while preserving signaling potency. For H2, carrier technologies may increase local residence time or allow combination with other therapeutics. In principle, these tools also enable sequence-specific multi-gas strategies, although that possibility remains underexplored (Figure 5).

sections.title: Biomarkers, Mechanistic Bottlenecks, and Experimental Priorities

paragraphs.en: One reason mechanistic debates persist is that the field still lacks sufficiently precise in vivo readouts. Many studies infer gas action from downstream antioxidant enzyme expression, total glutathione, or bulk oxidative stress markers. These are useful but indirect. A stronger mechanistic program requires real-time or residue-resolved detection of S-nitrosylation, persulfidation, oxidized phospholipid mediators, and subcellular redox shifts in the same biological system.3940

For Nrf2 specifically, researchers often stop at nuclear translocation or induction of HO-1, NQO1, or GCLC. These markers are important but not sufficient to distinguish canonical Keap1 cysteine sensing from noncanonical autophagy- or kinase-driven activation. Nor can they separate direct gas chemistry from secondary changes in mitochondrial function or inflammatory burden. Future work should therefore combine transcriptional readouts with residue-level Keap1 modification mapping, reporter systems for compartmental redox status, and experimental designs that manipulate upstream kinases or autophagy nodes in parallel.

Acute injury trials may prioritize organ-function recovery, inflammatory biomarkers, and mitochondrial injury markers. Chronic disease studies may need repeated measurements of metabolic flexibility, endothelial function, imaging, and transcriptomic adaptation. Because Nrf2 is a network regulator, success may be missed if evaluation focuses too narrowly on one antioxidant enzyme or one plasma oxidative marker. A biomarker strategy that reflects pathway breadth will better match the biology of gas-mediated adaptation. Comparative studies are harder to perform, but they are essential. Only by testing NO, H2S, and H2 side by side under matched injury models, matched delivery conditions, and matched pathway assays can researchers determine where convergence is real, where mechanisms diverge, and where combination logic is justified. A Nrf2-centered framework provides the structure for such comparisons, but careful experimentation must supply the evidence.

Most available evidence is preclinical, and substantial heterogeneity exists in experimental models, gas donors, delivery methods, doses, and outcome measures. Direct comparisons among NO, H2S, and H2 remain limited, while some proposed mechanisms, particularly those involving H2, are supported mainly by indirect evidence.

NO, H2S, and H2 do not converge on the Nrf2/Keap1 axis by identical routes. NO and H2S are redox-active signaling molecules whose access to Keap1 is grounded in direct or near-direct cysteine chemistry, whereas H2 appears to influence the pathway mainly through indirect remodeling of oxidative propagation, mitochondrial function, and stress-responsive signaling networks.111922 Recognizing this asymmetry is essential for accurate mechanistic interpretation.

At the same time, these differences do not negate convergence. The three gases repeatedly stabilize overlapping adaptive states characterized by improved antioxidant defense, preserved mitochondrial quality, reduced inflammatory amplification, and enhanced stress tolerance. Nrf2 is a central translator of these states because it connects thiol sensing to transcriptional programs governing detoxification, metabolism, proteostasis, and organelle homeostasis.332

The most useful conceptual advance is therefore to view therapeutic gases not as interchangeable antioxidants, but as members of an interacting gas signaling network with distinct dominant chemistries and partially shared downstream architecture. It also emphasizes that future progress depends less on rhetorical claims of synergy and more on disciplined work defining timing, dose windows, delivery systems, and mechanistic biomarkers.
Open Questions
Which Keap1 cysteines are functionally modified by NO and H2S in vivo, and how context dependent are these modifications?
Does molecular hydrogen have a defined primary molecular target, or does it act mainly through distributed redox and metabolic modulation?
Under what conditions does crosstalk among NO, H2S, and H2 produce genuine therapeutic synergy?
